title: Cleaning Methods That Actually Work
subtitle: You know what to clean and who cleans it, but a target you dread is a target that waits. This chapter gives each one a method that is quick enough to actually do and good enough to actually work, so the list gets done instead of postponed.

They do not need to re-argue why we clean or to rebuild the list or reassign owners; they need each target to have a way of being cleaned that is quick enough to actually do and good enough to actually work, so a shared plan becomes a home that actually gets cleaned and read instead of a list people feel bad about.
core_promise: Close the gap between a target that is owned and a target that is clean by giving each one a working method. Learn that a method must be BOTH effective (the surface actually comes clean and you can read its condition) and easy (quick and painless enough that you will genuinely do it again), and that the best method is the one you will actually do. Use five working methods that lift almost any target toward quick-and-good: right tool for the surface; top to bottom, dry before wet; fewer, simpler products; keep the tool where the target is; clean in passing. Recognize dread as a method problem rather than a personal failing, keep the methods serving inspection so the target is cleaned and read in the same easy pass, and apply the treatment to the list you already have without changing a line of it or reassigning a single owner.

No shame: dreading a cleaning job is a method problem, not a character flaw; the reader is not lazy, they were handed slow methods, by habit and by how they were taught. The payoff is that dread drains out of a job the moment the method gets quick, with no change in character required; nobody has to become a more disciplined person to keep a clean home. worked_example.space: The whole home's Shine list from Chapter 17, and the launch pad within it. Instead of remaking the list or reassigning anyone, the reader gives each target a working method and applies the treatment to a worked set of two or three targets, so the same list becomes doable. Nothing on the list changes; every target is one already listed and already owned. All that changes is that each now has a way of being cleaned that is quick enough to actually do and good enough to actually work, and each, done that way, puts the eyes on the surface as the hand does the job.
worked_example.note: This chapter gives each target its how; it does not rebuild the Shine list or reassign owners (Chapter 17), does not re-argue why we clean beyond a callback (Chapter 16), does not build the repeatable routine, reset, or schedule (Chapter 19), and does not write standard-work documents or maintenance-over-time systems (Standardize and Sustain). Clean in passing is a method for a single target, not the whole-home routine. Source: Seiso Shine step 2, determine cleaning methods, home-scaled and referenced lightly, not overclaimed beyond Toyota and the Toyota Production System.

working_methods.right_tool_for_the_surface: Match the method to the material. The right cloth, the right brush, the right cheap scraper does in one easy pass what a paper towel and determination do in ten, because most struggle at the sink is really the wrong tool applied with extra effort.
working_methods.top_to_bottom_dry_before_wet: Order is free speed. Dust and crumbs fall, so clean the high things before the low ones, and do the dry jobs before the wet ones; work the other way and you dirty what you just cleaned and do half of it twice.
working_methods.fewer_simpler_products: A cupboard of specialist sprays is slower, not faster, because you spend the time choosing and reaching and running out. A small handful of simple products covers almost everything, costs less, is safer around children, and is simple enough that you actually restock it and use it.
working_methods.keep_the_tool_where_the_target_is: Storing each target's tool at the target removes the largest hidden cost of cleaning, which is the effort of starting. A cloth kept by the sink gets used; the same cloth in a cupboard down the hall does not. This is the point-of-use idea from Straighten, pointed at Shine.
working_methods.clean_in_passing: The cheapest clean is the one you never had to make time for, because you did it while you were already there: a wipe of the shower wall while the water runs, the counter while the pasta boils. Folded into a moment you were spending anyway, a small clean costs almost nothing and keeps a target from ever needing a big session.

worked_example.applied_pass: Pick two or three targets and give each the working-method treatment. The launch pad gets a single cloth kept in the entry drawer, right where the target is, so wiping the shelf and checking the hooks is a ten-second thing done in passing, not a job to schedule. A dreaded oven gets a gentler method left to sit while you do something else, fewer products and far less effort for the same clean result, instead of an hour of caustic scrubbing on your knees. The door handles need no method grander than the cloth already in your hand as you pass, wiped in a second and read in the same second.
worked_example.tally: Same list, same owners, nothing added and nothing reassigned, but each target now has a method quick enough to do and good enough to work, and each, done that way, put the eyes on the surface as the hand did the job: the same list, suddenly doable. Because the targets actually got cleaned across the home, grease that was on the hob is gone, grubby handles are clean and read, a dreaded oven is a done oven, the room's condition genuinely changed, so the friction meter follows Chapter 17's dashed forward projection and takes its next Shine step toward calm. It is a real step and not the finish of Shine; the goal is still ahead, because nothing yet makes the methods happen on their own, week after week, which is the next chapter.

definition: A working method is the quickest effective way to clean and read a given target: effective enough that the surface actually comes clean and shows what it needs, and easy enough that you will do it again without dreading it.
rule: The best method is the one you will actually do.
support_line: You do not have a cleaning problem. You have a method problem.
one_idea_to_keep: The best method is the one you will actually do. Match a quick, effective method to each target, keep it small enough to fold into an ordinary day, and Shine stops being a dreaded event and becomes a handful of easy passes that keep the whole home clean and read.
